note: Tool-command cases call the same pinned handler down both arms, over the same fixture, so the replies are compared whole; a bespoke CLI answers in its own shape and is projected onto the same fact. Every snowflake projection ends in `grep .`, so an arm whose reply carries no such line fails the case instead of agreeing on nothing.

cases.name: emails_get_folders
cases.why: both arms list the same IMAP folders

cases.name: emails_get_emails
cases.why: the same messages, in the same order, through either arm

cases.name: emails_search_emails
cases.why: a search returns the same hits

cases.name: snowflake_read_query
cases.why: the same statement returns the same answer through either arm

args.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS N FROM SLA_MONITOR.PUBLIC.SUPPORT_TICKETS

mirage.command: snowflake read-query '{"query":"SELECT COUNT(*) AS N FROM SLA_MONITOR.PUBLIC.SUPPORT_TICKETS"}'

cases.name: write_query
cases.why: a ticket closed through either arm leaves the same tables behind

args.query: UPDATE SLA_MONITOR.PUBLIC.SUPPORT_TICKETS SET STATUS = 'closed' WHERE TICKET_NUMBER = 'TK-1000'

mirage.command: snowflake write-query '{"query":"UPDATE SLA_MONITOR.PUBLIC.SUPPORT_TICKETS SET STATUS = '\''closed'\'' WHERE TICKET_NUMBER = '\''TK-1000'\''"}'

cases.note: every timestamp is placed relative to the warehouse clock at seed time, and the two arms are seeded a minute apart
